title: KPI Interchange Format (KIF) v1.0
description: The one contract between a tracker adapter and the KPI engine. An adapter's only job is to emit a valid KIF document. Everything downstream - KPI values, notes, the workbook, the PMS payload - is computed from this and never talks to the tracker. Unknown facts are null, never guessed: the engine reports 'Not measured' with a reason instead of inventing a number.

generated.description: Provenance. Written by the adapter so a reader can tell where the numbers came from.

source_url.description: Board / project URL the data came from.

capabilities.description: What this adapter could actually observe. A capability that is absent makes every KPI that depends on it 'Not measured' with a stated reason, rather than a wrong number. See adapters/_contract.md.

warnings.description: Anything the adapter could not resolve, in plain language. Surfaced to the user in the review step.

tracker.description: Human name of the tracker, e.g. 'Asana', 'Jira'.

pms_project_id.description: PMS project id. Null until the profile supplies one.

client_date.description: Project-level fallback: date the client expects delivery (YYYY-MM-DD).

commit_date.description: Project-level fallback: date the team committed to.

client_check.description: Handover = the client date is met when the period's handover build reached the client by the date. Delivery = met when the item itself was delivered by the date (use for a feature freeze where bug fixes may follow).

dates_why.description: Why these dates are the agreed ones, with links. Shown in the workbook, never sent to PMS.

sources_text.description: Where scope and hours came from, as '[words](url)' markdown.

periods.description: One entry per PMS period, in order. A project with no period structure has exactly one, usually named 'Full Project'.

name.description: Stable period name. PMS length limits are checked before delivery, never by truncating join keys.

old_name.description: Set when the period exists in PMS under a different name; the push renames it.

handover_date.description: Date the period's build reached the client. Null = not handed over yet, which the notes say out loud.

team_hours.description: Team-level effort not attributable to one item (bug fixing, regression, QA support) counted in Velocity.

plan_client_date.description: What the original plan said, kept for the 'Original plan: ...' remark when an agreed date differs.

notes.description: The period's story in the workbook, with '[words](url)' links.

plan_text.description: What the original plan said, with links.

tasks.description: One row per unit of deliverable work. Excluded rows stay in the list with type 'Excluded' and a reason, so the workbook can show what was left out and why.

key.description: Ticket key as humans say it. Falls back to the tracker id when the team has no key convention.

type.description: Task = in the agreed plan. CR = an approved addition after the plan. Scope = in-scope work that is neither (e.g. planned feedback handling). Excluded = not our deliverable.

planned.description: Was this in the initial scope of its period.

hours_qa.description: Counted into Velocity only once the item's QA is done.

hours_source.description: 'Project plan', 'Estimates sheet', 'Tracker estimate' - so a reader knows which number won.

delivered.description: Date the item reached the team's delivery event (profile workflow.delivered_when). Null = not delivered yet.

status.description: Tracker status as-is, for the reader.

understood.description: Requirement understood without going back to the client. Null = no history of its own, left out of the denominator.

met_client_date.description: Pending = not there yet and the date has not passed; left out of the denominator.

met_commitment.description: Did this item meet the date the team committed to. Null = the team made no commitment on it, which leaves it out of Delivery Commitment entirely - that KPI measures the reliability of promises made, so an item nobody promised is not evidence either way. Pending = committed but not yet due.

commit_date.description: The date the team negotiated and committed to for this item. Its presence is what makes the item part of Delivery Commitment.

reopened.description: Closed, then reopened. A QA fail while the item is still being tested for the first time is not rework.

remarks.description: Anything a reader needs, with '[words](url)' links.

defects.description: One row per reported issue, including the ones that will not be counted - the notes name what was left out and why.

kind.description: Only Bug counts by default; the counting policy can include Observation and Improvement.

phase.description: Post-release = found by the client or users after the handover build. Drives Escaped Defect Rate.

pre_existing.description: Already in the product before this work. Not counted by default.

rejected.description: Invalid, by design, duplicate, not reproducible, not feasible. Never counted as a defect.

against_task.description: Task key the defect was found against, when the tracker records it.

review.description: Judgement calls the adapter could not make on its own. The run skill turns these into one round of questions instead of many.

subject.description: Ticket key or period name the question is about.

proposal.description: What the adapter would do if nobody answers. Always offer one.
